newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand plans help for depressed property sector.
newsitem.headline: Thailand plans help for depressed property sector.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand plans to introduce additional measures such as soft loans to rescue the nation's depressed property sector, a senior central bank official said on Thursday.

Thirachai Phuvanatnalanubala, head of the central bank's Financial Institutions Supervision and Development Department, said lack of cashflow remained a big problem for the sector and financial institutions could still lend more to the sector.
"Even though the government has relaxed rules on loans and set no official limit, financial institutions are still cautious about extending the loans," he told a seminar on the property business.
He added that measures the bank planned to use to help the sector included providing soft loans to those wanting to buy houses by setting up a secondary mortgage agency to provide the loans.
It also establish a scheme in which some major financial institutions would help solve debt problems of other institutions hit by troubled loans to the property sector, he added.
"But debtors must also cooperate in providing information. We have done that with big debtors. The next step would involve medium and small ones," he said.
